rationale: C03 is a highly plausible direct drafting template. It uses the same complete list of tax-return types, the same year-and-Congress limitation structure, inspection by a congressional committee or authorized subcommittee, a purpose-specific investigation clause, and—most distinctively—the same reference to Treasury Decision 6064 as approved on February 11, 1954. The child largely preserves this machinery and wording while substituting the House Committee on Education and Labor, a narrower year range, and a welfare-and-pension-fund purpose. C06 and C07 share much of the standard structure but lack the child's distinctive Treasury Decision 6064 reference and are therefore weaker.

shared_material.child_excerpt: any income, excess-profits, declared value excess-profits, capital stock, estate, or gift tax return for the years 1947 to 1953, inclusive
shared_material.parent_excerpt: any income, excess-profits, declared value excess-profits, capital stock, estate, or gift tax return for the years 1942 to 1953, inclusive
shared_material.explanation: The same unusually detailed enumeration and date-range syntax are preserved, with only the starting year changed.

shared_material.child_excerpt: shall, during the Eighty-third Congress, be open to inspection by the Committee on Education and Labor of the House of Representatives, or any duly authorized subcommittee thereof
shared_material.parent_excerpt: shall, during the 83d Congress, be open to inspection by the Senate Banking and Currency Committee, or any duly authorized subcommittee thereof
shared_material.explanation: The child retains the operative congressional-inspection framework while replacing the designated committee.

shared_material.child_excerpt: subject to the conditions stated in Treasury Decision 6064, relating to inspection of returns by certain committees of the Congress, approved by me February 11, 1954
shared_material.parent_excerpt: in accordance and upon compliance with the rules and regulations prescribed by the Secretary of the Treasury in Treasury Decision 6064, relating to the inspection of returns by certain committees of the Congress, approved by me February 11, 1954
shared_material.explanation: The identical decision number, description, and approval date provide especially concrete evidence of reuse.

shared_material.child_excerpt: This Executive order shall be effective upon its filing for publication in the FEDERAL REGISTER.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: This Executive order shall be effective upon its filing for publication in the FEDERAL REGISTER.
shared_material.explanation: The same effectiveness clause completes the parallel operative sequence, though it is routine standing alone.
